newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Watermelon takes a slice off Israeli inflation.
newsitem.headline: Watermelon takes a slice off Israeli inflation.

text.p: Economists have cheered the unexpectedly low 0.7 percent rise in Israel's April consumer price index.
But others suspect pulp fiction. Watermelon prices were not included in the index, which according to at least one economist shaved 0.2 percentage points from the CPI.

"If they had measured watermelon like they have every other year, there would have been a 120 percent increase, which would have added 0.2 point," said Jonathan Katz, chief economist at Solid Financial Markets.
The inflation rate is not just an academic issue in Israel, where everything from wages to bond prices are linked to the official CPI.

A spokesman for the government's Central Bureau of Statistics said the fruit's weighting in the consumer price index is a mere 0.015 percent and its inclusion would have caused virtually no change to the CPI.

Watermelon has regularly appeared in the April index over the last few years, which is what caught many inflation observers off guard. It was sliced from this year's calculation because there was not enough around to count.

"A particular product gets into the index if during the month we find a certain minimum number of stores carrying it," the spokesman said, denying that the fruit was being manipuated to keep inflation down.
"We treat watermelon as we treat any other product," he declared. Blame bad weather for the late harvest, he added.

Watermelon is now in abundance and prices have been falling, which should help keep the CPI low this month, Bank Hapoalim said in its monthly inflation report. It is predicting a 0.9 percent rise in May.
Will Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel have his eye on the produce counter when he decides interest rates later this month?

"Watermelon had its effect, but there were other positive effects," said Katz, who said he was looking for an 0.3 point cut on the 13.9 percent base rate mainly because underlying inflation has been falling.
